He went to his family and said: "Wrap me up, wrap me up," and his limbs were trembling. Then Jibril came to him and said: "Read!" He said: "I am not a reader." Jibril pressed him until he reached his limit of exertion, while he was struggling with him to read, so he read (ﷺ).

Then {the mountains} – the firmly rooted, solid, hard ones – will become {kathiban mahilan} (a heap of sand, pouring down and scattered); that is, they will be like sand that flows and scatters. Then after that they will be pulverized and become like {al-habā' al-manthur} (scattered dust).

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 73, verses 15–16:

{15–16} He, exalted is He, says: Praise your Lord for sending this Prophet, the unlettered Arab, the bringer of good tidings and the warner, the witness over the nation concerning their deeds. Be thankful to him, stand up to this great blessing, and beware lest you disbelieve, disobeying your Messenger and becoming like Pharaoh when Allah sent to him Musa, son of Imran. He called him to Allah and commanded him to monotheism, but Pharaoh did not believe him; rather, he disobeyed him, so Allah seized him with ﴿a severe seizing﴾; that is, a harsh and painful seizing.

This is the commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 73, verse 19:

{19} That is: this admonition, through which Allah has informed about the conditions of the Day of Resurrection and its terrors, is a reminder by which the God-conscious (al-muttaqun) are mindful and by which the believers are restrained. {Whoever wills takes a path to his Lord}; that is, a way that leads to Him, and this is by following His law (shar'), for He has made it clear in the fullest clarity and set it forth in the most complete manifestation. In this is evidence that Allah, exalted is He, empowered His servants over their actions and enabled them to perform them, not as the Jabriyyah (determinists) say, that their actions occur without their will; for this contradicts both transmitted texts and reason.

{20} God mentioned at the beginning of this surah that He commanded His Messenger to stand in prayer for half the night, or two-thirds of it, or a third of it. The principle is that his community follows him in the rulings. In this verse He mentions that he complied with that, along with a group of believers with him. Since determining the exact time commanded was a hardship for people, He informed them that He had made it extremely easy for them. So He said: ﴿And God determines the night and the day﴾; that is, He knows their measures and what passes and what remains of them. ﴿He knew that you would not be able to count it﴾; that is, you would not be able to know its exact measure, neither more nor less, because that would require added alertness and exertion. That is, He lightened it for you and commanded you with what is easy for you, whether it exceeds the estimated measure or falls short of it. ﴿So recite what is easy of the Qur'an﴾; that is, what you know and what is not difficult for you. For this reason, the one who prays at night is commanded to pray as long as he is energetic. When he tires, grows lazy, or becomes drowsy, let him rest, so that he may perform the prayer with tranquility and ease.

Then He mentioned some of the reasons suitable for lightening the obligation, so He said: ﴿He knew that there would be among you those who are ill﴾: for them, praying half the night, or two-thirds of it, or a third of it, is difficult. So the sick person should pray what is easy for him, and he is not commanded to stand in prayer when that is burdensome. Indeed, if voluntary prayer is hard for him, he may abandon it, and he still receives the reward of what he used to do while healthy. ﴿And others travelling through the land seeking of God's bounty﴾; that is, He knew that among you there would be travellers who journey for trade, to become self-sufficient and to avoid depending on people. The traveller's condition suits lightening the obligation. For this reason, leniency is granted to him in obligatory prayer: he is permitted to combine two prayers at one time, and to shorten the four-rak'ah prayer. Likewise, ﴿others fighting in the way of God, so recite what is easy of it﴾. Thus, He mentioned two kinds of lightening: a lightening for the healthy resident, who observes his energy without being burdened with determining the exact time, but instead seeks the excellent prayer, which is the third of the night after its first half; and a lightening for the sick and the traveller, whether his travel is for trade or for worship, such as jihad, hajj, or other things. For he [also] observes what does not burden him. So praise and thanks be to God, who has not placed hardship upon us in the religion, but has made His law easy and has considered the conditions of His servants and the interests of their religion, their bodies, and their worldly affairs.

Then He commanded the servants with two acts of worship, which are the mother of acts of worship and its pillars: establishing the prayer (salah), without which the religion cannot stand, and giving zakat (almsgiving), which is the proof of faith and through which compassion is shown to the poor and the needy. So He said: ﴿And establish the prayer﴾; that is, with its pillars, its limits, its conditions, and all its complements. ﴿And lend God a goodly loan﴾; that is, sincerely for the sake of God's countenance, with a true intention, steadfastness of the soul, and good wealth. This includes obligatory and recommended charity.

Then He urged the general doing of good and its deeds, so He said: ﴿And whatever good you send forward for yourselves, you will find it with God, better and greater in reward﴾: a good deed is rewarded tenfold, up to seven hundred times, up to many multiples. Let it be known that an atom's weight of good in this world is matched by multiples of multiples of this world and all that is in it, in the abode of lasting bliss, with its pleasures and desires. And goodness and righteousness in this worldly life are the seed of goodness and righteousness in the abode of permanence, its root and foundation. Alas for the times that passed in heedlessness! Alas for the eras that elapsed in other than righteous deeds! Alas for hearts upon which the admonition of their Creator has had no effect, and in which the encouragement of One more merciful to them than themselves has not benefited! O God, to You belongs all praise, to You is the complaint, in You is the refuge, and there is no power and no strength except through You. ﴿And seek God's forgiveness; indeed God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. In the command to seek forgiveness after the urging toward acts of obedience and good, there is great benefit. That is because the servant is never free of shortcoming in what he has been commanded: either he does not do it at all, or he does it in a deficient manner. So he is commanded to mend that with seeking forgiveness, for the servant sins by night and by day. Whenever God does not cover him with His mercy and forgiveness, he is ruined.

The tafsir is complete, and praise belongs to God.
